claims.text: W–Cu composites produced by conventional powder-metallurgy routes often have nonuniform interfacial contact, residual voids, and phase segregation.
Poor W–Cu interfacial wetting causes or contributes to nonuniform contact, voids, and phase segregation.
All tungsten surfaces will be coated with a nanoscale copper layer by vapor deposition before spark-plasma sintering.
A thin, uniform vapor-deposited copper coating will promote near-perfect W–Cu interfacial bonding during spark-plasma sintering.
The copper coating will minimize void formation during consolidation.
The copper coating will reduce interfacial-energy mismatch between W and Cu.
The coating will produce a more uniform, defect-scarce W–Cu microstructure.
The copper coating will enhance W–Cu wettability during spark-plasma sintering.
The copper coating will enhance diffusion bonding by ensuring continuous contact across W–Cu interfaces.
Improved interfacial contact will reduce phase separation and void formation during thermal cycling and irradiation.
Reduced interfacial defects will maintain effective thermal transport under thermal cycling and irradiation.
Reduced interfacial defects will preserve mechanical durability under fusion-reactor conditions.
Relative to uncoated W–Cu made by conventional spark-plasma sintering or mechanical alloying, coated material will have a lower void fraction.
Relative to the uncoated baseline, coated material will have higher interfacial integrity.
Relative to the uncoated baseline, coated material will have higher thermal conductivity.
Relative to the uncoated baseline, coated material will maintain or improve mechanical strength under irradiation.
Effectiveness depends on obtaining a uniform, adherent copper coating on tungsten particles at industrially relevant scale.
Effectiveness depends on the copper coating remaining stable during high-temperature consolidation and irradiation cycling.
The magnitude of thermal and mechanical improvements under fusion-relevant irradiation remains quantitatively undetermined.
